entries.content: IG* = IG - RY_i + ABR. Productive investment is gross private domestic investment adjusted by subtracting royalties in investment (RY_i) and adding back an adjustment for business receipts (ABR). This isolates the investment flows that contribute to productive capital accumulation.
NIPA source: Table 1.1.5 line 6 provides gross private domestic investment (IG). Royalty and ABR adjustments come from supplementary NIPA tables. Book data in Table E.2.
IG* appears in Table E.2 as part of the demand-side revenue account. No dedicated figure. Feeds into the investment/accumulation analysis of Chapter 9.

RY_i (royalties in investment) represents resource rents embedded in investment goods, which are transfers rather than productive value creation. ABR (adjustment for business receipts) reconciles the NIPA investment measure with the Marxian productive investment concept.
The ABR adjustment is specific to the NIPA accounting framework of the book period. Modern NIPA revisions may require recalculating this adjustment. NIPA line 6 references need vintage verification.
I*G = {IG} - RYi  (IVA merged into value added on revenue side, hence into I*G on use side)
entries.context: Canonical formula for S509. Productive investment equals NIPA gross private domestic investment minus royalties in investment. Footnote 4 documents that the inventory valuation adjustment (IVA) is merged into value added on the revenue side and thus into I*G on the use side. The ABR adjustment is added in annual estimates per page 91.

entries.content: Building and equipment rental: Merged into total trade sector; NOT unbundled; NOT adjusted for amortization of building and equipment rented out (ABR) in benchmark IO tables. In annual NIPA estimates (Section 5.2): ABR adjustment IS incorporated.
entries.context: Establishes the ABR (amortization of building and equipment rented out) adjustment regime for S509: NOT present in benchmark IO estimates (Table 5.2) but IS incorporated in the annual NIPA-based series (Table 5.4) that S509 replicates. This determines whether RMWND P02 must add ABR depending on which book table is being matched.

entries.content: Take from NIPA directly: {CON, IG, X-IM, G, WG}. Interpolate between benchmarks: M's, RYs, and ROWs. Assemble to form TP*: Calculate remaining components and assemble together.
entries.context: Three-step use-side construction protocol for S509: IG comes DIRECTLY from NIPA Table 1.1.5 line 6, while the RYi deduction is interpolated from benchmark IO data using receiving-industry GVA as numeraire (per page 96). Defines the L01 -> P02 ordering for the productive investment series.

entries.content: I*G = {IG} − RYi (IVA merged into value added on revenue side, hence into I*G on use side).
entries.context: Section 5.2, p. 95 + Footnote 4: exact formula for productive investment used in S509. S509 reports IG* = IG - RY_i + ABR (with ABR for the annual series consistent with Table 5.4).

entries.content: Building and equipment rental: Merged into total trade sector; NOT unbundled; NOT adjusted for amortization of building and equipment rented out (ABR) in benchmark IO tables… In annual NIPA estimates (Section 5.2): ABR adjustment IS incorporated.
entries.context: Section 5.1 (p. 91): documents the ABR adjustment used in the annual S509 series — not present in benchmark IO tables but applied to NIPA-based annual estimates.

entries.content: For royalties RY we use the receiving industry's GVA (i.e. GVAry) as the numeraire, as in xi ≡ (RYi/GVAry)_IO. This is done because some royalties such as RYi and RYx-im appear as components of highly unstable final-demand totals like I or X-IM (see Figure 5.1). Benchmark coefficients created by dividing these royalties by unstable totals are not very useful.
entries.context: Section 5.2, p. 96: interpolation methodology for RYi, the royalty-payment component subtracted from IG to obtain IG*.

methodology_summary: Productive investment adjusts gross private domestic investment: IG* = IG - RY_i + ABR. NIPA Table 1.1.5 line 6 is the primary source. Book period from Table E.2.
known_issues: NIPA line numbers may shift across vintages
ABR adjustment methodology may need updating for modern NIPA
No dedicated figure in the book
